description: Enrico Gabrielli (born 24 October 1976, Montevarchi, Arezzo, Italy) is an Italian multi-instrumentalist, composer, arranger, producer, and writer. Also known by his pseudonym Der Maurer, he is a central node in Italy's experimental/library/psychedelic underground. A graduate of the Conservatorio G. Verdi di Milano (clarinet), he has contributed to over 250 recordings in a 25+ year career. He is best known as a founding member of Calibro 35 (cinematic funk), The Winstons (progressive rock), and as the creator of the 19'40" recording series. His work spans psychedelic funk, chamber composition, film/TV scoring, and children's music (Le Canzonine, 2023). He is also a novelist, debuting with the mystery novel Virginia (Wudz Edizioni, 2024).

historical_significance: Founding member of Calibro 35 — pioneering cinematic funk band whose music was sampled by Dr. Dre (Compton), Jay Z, Damon Albarn
Calibro 35 performed at the closing ceremony of the Milano-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics
Created 19'40" recording series — a subscription-based, small-run CD series mirroring demotape ethos
Bridge figure between Italian contemporary classical, psychedelic funk, progressive rock, and library music revival
Contributed to 250+ recordings over 25+ years as session musician and collaborator
Film/TV scoring includes RAI series Blanca and Sandokan, Diabolik (Manetti Bros), collaborations with Arthur Harari (Oscar winner)
Arranged music for Iggy Pop's 2023 Mantua performance with Orchestra da Camera di Mantova
Children's music album 'Le Canzonine' (2023) praised for artistic depth beyond genre expectations
Debut mystery novel 'Virginia' (2024) expands his artistic profile beyond music
Central node connecting Italian underground artists: Zu, Aucan, Morkobot, Julie's Haircut, Hobocombo via Esecutori di Metallo su Carta
milan_scene_context: Enrico Gabrielli is a central figure in Milan's experimental music scene, operating at the intersection of conservatory-trained composition, psychedelic funk, and underground experimentalism. Based in Milan, he works from Laboratori Testone (engineered by Tommaso Colliva) and collaborates with the Bologna axis (Vacuum Studio/Bruno Germano). His 19'40" label operates on a subscription model that mirrors demotape culture — small runs, direct-to-listener, curatorially driven. While not part of the 1985-2000 Florentine/Milanese underground timeline that defines the project's core scope, his work exists in the same genealogical space: obscure Italian library music, analog synthesis, small-batch physical releases, and the bridging of high-concept composition with underground aesthetics.
current_activity: As of 2025, Enrico Gabrielli is highly active: releasing Der Maurer Vol. 2 (April 2025), touring with Calibro 35 (Ellroy vs L.A. OST, Exploration album), continuing 19'40" series (14th release Ghosts Goblins Ghouls), and working on the third season of Blanca (RAI series) and the 2025 Sandokan remake.

literary_work.description: Debut mystery novel set in an old fascist-era villa turned nursing home in the Valdarno area (Tuscany). Gothic-tinged mystery with eccentric characters.
literary_work.significance: Reflects Gabrielli's broader artistic range — a multiform talent operating across music, composition, and literature.

notes: Enrico Gabrielli is a hub figure in Italy's experimental music network. While his active career (2000-present) falls partly outside the project's 1985-2000 core scope, his aesthetic universe (vintage synths, analog recording, Italian library music, obscure composition) and connections to underground artists make him highly relevant. His 19'40" label is a direct parallel to demotape culture. 4 key connections documented: Calibro 35 (core), The Winstons (core), Julie's Haircut (collaboration via Esecutori di Metallo su Carta), Junkfood (collaboration). Additional session work with PJ Harvey, Mike Patton, Muse, Iggy Pop, Afterhours documented.
